requirement: Password hashing and verification utility implementing secure PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with cryptographically random 16-byte salt, constant-time verification via hmac.compare_digest, non-empty password validation, and explicit rejection of weak digests (MD5, SHA1).
skeleton: PasswordHasher class with hash_password and verify_password using hashlib and hmac.

rationale.teaches: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with a fresh 16-byte random salt per hash, constant-time verification, an empty-password guard, and refusal of MD5 and SHA1.
rationale.why: Any digest function produces a hex string that round-trips through verify, so the algorithm choice is invisible to a verify-only test. The fixture decodes the stored format and re-derives with PBKDF2 to confirm the algorithm and that two hashes of the same password differ.

candidates.why_wrong: MD5 replaces PBKDF2, so the stored hash is fast to brute-force and does not match a PBKDF2 re-derivation.
SHA1 replaces PBKDF2, so the hash has no work factor and does not match a PBKDF2 re-derivation.
A fixed salt is used for every password, so two users with the same password get identical hashes.
Verification uses == instead of compare_digest, so the comparison time leaks how many leading bytes match.
An empty password is hashed instead of rejected, so an account can be created with no password.
